clue.text: King having coronation

parts.note: CR, for the Latin Carolus Rex, is a standard abbreviation for king
having something means owning it

explanation.surface: A monarch going through his coronation ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: The crowning of a monarch is the ceremony itself, so the two nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: One holds garment firm on a dog

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
to dog someone is to follow or track them

explanation.surface: A business with a hound wearing a coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A coatrack is a stand of hooks or pegs for hanging coats, so it holds a garment.

clue.text: Old fluids in pens which pigs emit

parts.note: the liquids in fountain pens are inks

explanation.surface: Pigs in their pens leaking old fluids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pens' looks like pigsties, but it means writing pens.
explanation.definitionFit: Oinks are the grunting noises that pigs make, the sounds they emit.

clue.text: Further broadcast in hours

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A programme put out again for further hours.
explanation.definitionFit: To further and to nourish both mean to promote the growth or development of something.

clue.text: Condition institution for cons

definitions.meaning: British idiom: in good ... means in good condition
British slang for a prison or police station

explanation.surface: The state of a prison for convicts.
explanation.definitionFit: Nick is British slang both for a state of repair and for a jail where convicts are held.

clue.text: Decline accompanying soldiers in retreat

parts.note: to be accompanying someone is to be with them

indicators.note: an army in retreat goes backwards, so the soldiers' letters are read in reverse

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a common crossword abbreviation for soldiers

explanation.surface: An army's fortunes decline as its troops fall back.
explanation.definitionFit: To wither is to shrivel or fade away, a synonym of the verb decline.

clue.text: First, put up plait in individual clasps

indicators.note: in a down clue put up means the letters read upwards, in reverse
the words plait in individual clasp, that is hold within them, a run of letters

explanation.surface: Hair is pinned up first, a plait held in single clips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clasps' finds LAITINI in pLAIT IN Individual, and 'put up' reads it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Initial means coming at the beginning, the earliest, so it matches first as an adjective.

clue.text: Awful moans stifled by composer mounting carriage

indicators.note: one piece is muffled inside the other
in a down clue mounting means climbing upward, so the word reads in reverse

parts.note: Johann Sebastian Bach, the German composer

indicators.note: awful suggests something badly made, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Groans muffled as a composer climbs into a carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awful' scrambles the moans to ANSOM; 'mounting' turns the composer upside down in this down entry, and 'stifled by' tucks the scrambled groans inside him.
explanation.definitionFit: A hansom cab is a two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage with the driver seated behind.

clue.text: Foolhardy, heartless and hollow

indicators.note: without its heart, the central letters are removed

parts.note: reckless means foolhardy

explanation.surface: Someone foolhardy, cruel and empty inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A recess is a niche or hollowed-out space set into a wall.

clue.text: Reports of earnings regularly carrying little weight

indicators.note: the picked letters carry, that is hold within them, the other piece
taking letters at regular intervals, here every second letter of the word earnings

parts.note: an ounce is a small unit of weight

explanation.surface: Company reports of earnings that turn out to carry little weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reports' looks like a noun about company results but is the verb. 'regularly' picks every second letter, ANNS, and 'carrying' makes those letters hold the small weight.
explanation.definitionFit: To announce something is to make it known publicly, so reports as a verb is a synonym.

clue.text: One wrong handle lifted leads to alarm ringing

parts.note: a sin is a wrong

indicators.note: in a down clue lifted means raised up, read in reverse

parts.note: a lug is a projecting handle

indicators.note: leads are the first letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A single wrong lift of a handle sets an alarm ringing.
explanation.definitionFit: Singular means relating to only one, in grammar or in general.

clue.text: Superhuman removing leader of ancient people

indicators.note: the leading, first letter is taken off the word for superhuman

parts.note: bionic describes superhuman powers given by electronic body parts, as in the Bionic Man

explanation.surface: A superhuman being who drops the leader of some ancient tribe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader of ancient people' looks like one phrase, but 'leader' belongs to the wordplay and 'of ancient people' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ionic describes the Ionians, an ancient Greek people, and their order of architecture.

clue.text: Simple game with short cue

parts.note: RU stands for rugby union, a game

indicators.note: short means the word is cut by its final letter

parts.note: a cue is the stick used in snooker or pool

explanation.surface: A simple game of snooker played with a cut-down cue.
explanation.definitionFit: Rustic means plain and unsophisticated, like country life, so simple is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Neighbourhood against chains being put on little space

indicators.note: the other pieces are put on, that is placed after, the little space

parts.note: an en is a small printing space, half an em
V is short for versus, against
irons are fetters or chains

explanation.surface: Locals in a neighbourhood protest against being chained into a tiny space.
explanation.definitionFit: Environs are the surrounding district, the area round about, so neighbourhood is a synonym.

clue.text: Make pals with beer find rum

indicators.note: rum in British use means odd or strange, so the letters are put in a strange order

explanation.surface: Drinkers make friends with someone who finds beer and rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like another drink beside beer, but it is the old British word for odd.
explanation.definitionFit: To befriend someone is to become friends with them, to make pals.

clue.text: Country inn seen in artefact after analysis, we hear

indicators.note: after places the second part after the first in the answer
we hear signals that a word is given by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: a check is an examination or analysis

indicators.note: one piece is seen within the other

parts.note: a relic is a surviving artefact from the past
a pub is an inn

explanation.surface: A country inn turns up in an antique after some investigation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country inn' reads as one phrase but splits: 'Country' is the definition. 'we hear' applies only to the analysis word; 'seen in' and 'after' build the second word, which is spelt normally.
explanation.definitionFit: The Czech Republic is a country in central Europe, now often called Czechia.

clue.text: Attendants of European Republican deluged by questions …

indicators.note: the Republican is swamped by, inside, the questions

parts.note: queries are questions

explanation.surface: A European Republican's aides face a flood of questions.
explanation.definitionFit: Equerries are officers of the British royal household who attend members of the royal family.

clue.text: … wrongly press one for answer

indicators.note: wrongly means the letters are placed in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Hitting the wrong button on a quiz buzzer for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A response is a reply, an answer to a question.

clue.text: Exceptional bus plan's sure a hit

indicators.note: a hit knocks the letters about, so they are scrambled into a new order

explanation.surface: A transport proposal claimed to be an exceptional, sure-fire success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a hit' looks like praise for the plan, but it signals the anagram of BUS PLANS SURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unsurpassable cannot be beaten or bettered, so it is truly exceptional.

clue.text: That girl embracing university still rejected sleep

indicators.note: the girl's word holds the rest within it

parts.note: she means that girl

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the word reads in reverse

parts.note: yet means still, as in not yet

explanation.surface: A girl at university, still rebuffed, cannot sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns YET into TEY, and SHE embraces U and TEY.
explanation.definitionFit: Shut-eye is informal for sleep, the time spent with eyes closed.

clue.text: Glittering bridge above lake filling sides of gully

indicators.note: in a down clue above puts the bridge first

parts.note: to bridge something is to span it

indicators.note: the lake fills the space between the other letters
the sides are the outer letters only

explanation.surface: A sparkling scene of a bridge over a lake in a ravine.
explanation.definitionFit: Spangly means covered in spangles, small shiny sequins, so glittering.

clue.text: Fearing supernatural creature in picture

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other

parts.note: pic is short for picture
a hob is a hobgoblin, a mischievous sprite

explanation.surface: Someone frightened by a goblin in a photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: Phobic means having a phobia, an irrational fear.

clue.text: Perhaps Poirot's man given many tasks

definitions.meaning: Agatha Christie's detective is Hercule Poirot, so the possessive of his first name gives the answer, with perhaps hinting at the trick
the Greek hero who had to perform twelve labours

explanation.surface: Christie's detective as a man burdened with chores.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading treats the answer as HERCULE'S, the detective's forename plus possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: The hero of Greek myth was set twelve labours by King Eurystheus, many tasks indeed.

clue.text: Directive backing dock strike

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a law is a rule or directive
to dock is to cut off, to lop

explanation.surface: A directive supporting a strike by dockworkers.
explanation.definitionFit: A wallop is a heavy blow or hit, so it means strike, as noun or verb.

clue.text: Erected for one party, large shelter

indicators.note: in a down clue erected means built upwards, so the letters read in reverse

parts.note: EG, for example, means for one
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A large marquee put up for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A lodge is a small house or cabin, a place of refuge, so it is a shelter.

clue.text: Drink Rioja, not port, and case of Valpolicella

indicators.note: not means the port is left out of the wine's name

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a port in Brazil

indicators.note: the case is the outer letters, the shell of the word

explanation.surface: A wine lover's order: Rioja, no port, and a case of Valpolicella.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the fortified wine among the other wines, but it is a harbour city, Rio.
explanation.definitionFit: Java is informal, chiefly American, slang for coffee, a drink.

clue.text: Bung kid stuck in empty bottle

indicators.note: one piece is stuck inside the other
an empty word keeps only its outer letters, its contents removed

parts.note: to kid someone is to tease or rib them

explanation.surface: A child gets wedged inside an empty bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bung' looks like a stopper for the bottle, but it is British slang for a bribe.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a bung is an illicit payment, a bribe, as in football transfer scandals.

clue.text: Fellow nurses worn-out continued at length

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold closely, so one piece cradles the other

parts.note: a don is a fellow of a university college
ragged clothes are worn out

explanation.surface: A college fellow tends exhausted patients through a long shift.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that dragged on lasted tediously long, so continued at length is the idiom's sense.

clue.text: Overindulge in Greek island group

parts.note: Cos (Kos) is an island in the Dodecanese
a set is a group

explanation.surface: A party overindulging on a Greek island holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: To cosset is to pamper someone, to spoil or indulge them excessively.

clue.text: Good man eyed new moon

indicators.note: new tells us the letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A decent fellow gazes at a new moon.
explanation.definitionFit: Ganymede is the largest moon of Jupiter, named after the cupbearer of Greek myth.
